summary: Owned units s0267–s0288 date two calendrical settings in the Chinese: 太元中 for the Jiankang Taiji Hall plaque episode (Xie An asking Wang Xianzhi) and 魏時 for the Lingyun Hall scaffold anecdote about Wei Zhongjiang. Those era/dynasty labels convert, at year precision, to Eastern Jin Xiaowu Taiyuan AD 376–396 and Cao Wei AD 220–265; the year-only endpoints are conventional reign-year labels, not day-level Gregorian event dates (Taiyuan 21/XII and Xianxi 2/XII each run into the next Western January). Claim-675 correctly keeps 七八歲時 as an age and does not invent a birth year. The remaining closed Western intervals are not in the Chinese: 七八歲時學書 is an age, not 永和/升平 or AD 345–361; 桓溫嘗使書扇 is an undated 嘗; 以選尚新安公主 and the Wu-commandery garden visit are likewise undated, and both were given the unrelated sourceDate 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安 plus an invented AD 360–396 window. Context claim-690 uses that same unsupported visit window and is not accepted as Xie An life chronology. No owned unit states a birth or death for p089–p094.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi was seven or eight sui when he practiced calligraphy and his father could not tug the brush away.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xianzhi (p082). s0267 states only 七八歲時 for this practice scene. The row keeps that age as an age statement and does not convert inclusive sui into a birth year or a Western interval. Endpoints are not applicable.

evidence.quote: 七八歲時學書

itemChecks.event: During Taiyuan, Xie An wanted Wang Xianzhi to inscribe the newly raised Taiji Hall plaque; Xianzhi then soon received further offices.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xianzhi (p082). The dated act is the Taiyuan plaque episode in s0281; 尋 in s0291 only continues that narrative. 太元 here is Eastern Jin Xiaowu (司馬曜), not Wu or any later Taiyuan. Conventional era-year labels are 太元元年=AD 376 through 太元二十一年=AD 396; 隆安 begins the following first month. Those year-precision bounds describe uncertainty inside the named era, not a Gregorian day. Wikipedia’s table shows 太元二十一年十二月 beginning in January 397, which is why a reign-year label need not equal every month’s Western year.

evidence.quote: 太元中，新起太極殿，安欲使獻之題榜
尋除建威將軍、吳興太守，徵拜中書令。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi practiced calligraphy at seven or eight sui while his father tested his grip.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xianzhi (p082). The Chinese date is only 七八歲時, an age at the event, not a reign or year. AD 345–361 matches Emperor Mu’s 永和–升平 span and is not stated in s0267. Inventing both endpoints from an age (or from Xizhi’s famous years) violates the ban on converting inclusive age into a calendar window. The source date is unresolved unless left as age-only.

evidence.quote: 七八歲時學書，羲之密從後掣其筆不得

itemChecks.event: Xie An, during Taiyuan, wanted Wang Xianzhi to write the new Taiji Hall plaque as a lasting treasure.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Xie An (p089). s0281 places 安欲使獻之題榜 under 太元中. Endpoints AD 376 and AD 396 are the conventional first and last years of Eastern Jin Xiaowu’s Taiyuan era (polity 東晉, ruler 孝武帝司馬曜, era 太元, repeated name distinguished from Wu’s short Taiyuan). This is uncertainty about when in that era the request occurred, not a claim that Xie An was active in every year of the dynasty.

The closed interval treats Mu-era activity as if it dated this event and invents both endpoints from an age formula.

itemChecks.reason: Owner is Huan Wen (p091). s0269 gives 桓溫嘗使書扇: 嘗 is not an era, reign, or year. AD 345–373 is Huan Wen’s external career span, not a source window for this fan episode. A date window must date the event’s uncertainty, not stretch activity across a career. Both endpoints are invented; the source date is unresolved.

The sourceDate text 嘗與兄徽之、操之俱詣謝安 is Xianzhi’s visit to Xie An (s0258), a different episode and not her act. AD 360–396 invents both endpoints and does not describe uncertainty attested in s0270.

itemChecks.event: Xie An’s anecdote places Wei Dan (Wei Zhongjiang) in Wei, when he was made to write the already-nailed Lingyun Hall plaque.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wei Dan (p094). s0281 sets that story in 魏時. In this Eastern Jin speech, 魏 is Cao Wei (文帝曹丕 黄初 through 元帝曹奂 咸熙), not Northern Wei. Conventional year-labels are AD 220 (黄初元年, tenth month) and AD 265 (咸熙二年, last Wei year; 泰始 begins that same twelfth month). Year-precision 220–265 states uncertainty inside the named dynasty, not day-level Gregorian coverage; 咸熙二年十二月 begins in January 266. Xianzhi’s denial 甯有此事 is a competing reading of the anecdote’s truth, not of its Wei setting. The telling is Taiyuan; the claimed event remains Wei, not the reception date.

itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wei Dan (p094). The event is the Wei-period scaffold writing inside Xie An’s speech, dated 魏時, not the Taiyuan telling. Cao Wei year-labels AD 220–265 are the conventional first Huangchu year and last Xianxi year; they bound uncertainty about when in Wei the anecdote is set. Later reception is not used as a life date. Xianzhi’s 甯有此事 remains a competing witness about historicity.

references.title: 太元 (东晋)
references.quote: 寧康四年（376年）正月三日，改元為太元元年。
references.reason: Primary calendar check for 太元中: Eastern Jin Xiaowu, 寧康四年正月改元太元元年, conventional AD 376 start of the era-year label.

references.title: 太元 (东晋)
references.quote: 太元二十二年（397年）正月一日，改元為隆安元年。
references.reason: Confirms Taiyuan ends when 隆安元年 begins in the first month of 397, so the conventional last Taiyuan year-label is AD 396 (太元二十一年), not a day-level span through every month.

references.title: 黄初
references.quote: 黃初元年——十月二十九日，魏王曹丕稱帝，建立魏國。
references.reason: Confirms Cao Wei begins in 黄初元年 tenth month under 文帝曹丕, the conventional AD 220 year-label used for 魏時.

references.title: 咸熙
references.quote: 咸熙二年十二月，曹奂被迫禅位于司马炎。曹魏灭亡，晋朝建立。
references.reason: Confirms 咸熙 is Cao Wei’s last era and that the abdication falls in 咸熙二年十二月, the conventional AD 265 year-label for the dynasty’s end (that twelfth month overlaps January 266).
